draft.title: Travel across time zones
card: A flight takes the same real time whatever the clocks say. To find the arrival time, add the flight time to the departure time first.
Then adjust for the time difference between the two places. If the destination is ahead of where you left, add the difference. If it is behind, subtract it.
A flight leaves Sydney at 10:00 am and takes 3 hours. The destination is 2 hours behind Sydney.
10:00 am + 3 hours = 1:00 pm Sydney time. Then 1:00 pm − 2 hours = 11:00 am local time at the destination.
draft.remember: Add the flight time, then add or subtract the time difference.

a.q: A flight leaves Sydney at 8:00 am and takes 4 hours. The destination is 3 hours behind Sydney. What is the local arrival time?
a.why: 8:00 am + 4 hours = 12:00 noon Sydney time. The destination is behind, so subtract 3 hours to get 9:00 am. Adding the 3 hours gives 3:00 pm, which is wrong because a place that is behind has an earlier clock time.
a.clue: Add the flight time first, then use the time difference.

b.q: Jamal's flight leaves Sydney at 9:30 am and takes 9 hours. The destination is 2 hours ahead of Sydney. What is the local arrival time?
b.why: 9:30 am + 9 hours = 6:30 pm Sydney time. The destination is ahead, so add 2 hours to get 8:30 pm. Subtracting 2 hours gives 4:30 pm, which is wrong because a place that is ahead has a later clock time.
b.clue: Ahead means the clock there shows a later time.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: 9:00 am for (a) and 8:30 pm for (b), and the explanations match the card.
